title: The onion trade that looked profitable but wasn't

why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2023: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 20 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.

scenes.headline: January 2023
scenes.caption: Lasalgaon (Nashik) is India's best-known onion auction; Azadpur (Delhi) is the largest terminal market it feeds, a link the RBI paper describes.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 20 matched days, Lasalgaon reported a median ₹1,350 per quintal; Azadpur reported ₹1,350 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹50/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹50 per quintal and was positive on 70% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,115 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,115 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~13 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹240/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹349 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹486 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 0 of 20 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would not have shipped on any of 20 days.

scenes.headline: The lesson
